equation_request.abstract: We present several families of graphs that allow both efficient quantum walk implementations and efficient quantum walk based search algorithms. For these graphs, we construct quantum circuits that explicitly implement the full quantum walk search algorithm, without reference to a ‘black box’ oracle. These circuits provide a practically implementable method to explore quantum walk based search algorithms with the aim of eventual real-world applications. We also provide a numerical analysis of a quantum walk based search along a twisted toroid family of graphs, which requires O($\sqrt{n}$ log($n$)) elementary 2-qubit quantum gate operations to find a marked node.

specification.problem: Quantum-walk-based search for a marked node on an n-node graph, with the walk and marking implemented by explicit circuits rather than a black-box oracle. The abstract gives no graph definitions, walk operators or circuits.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Generic discrete-time (coined) quantum walk search on a tiny assumed instance, the 4-cycle (n=4, a 2-qubit position register). Only standard background equations are given. The paper's graph families, the twisted toroid construction, the explicit circuits and the numerical analysis are outside this scope.

symbols.domain: unitary on position and coin space

equations.label: Gate-count claim
equations.description: Elementary 2-qubit gate count for finding a marked node on the twisted toroid family
equations.abstract_quote: requires O($\sqrt{n}$ log($n$)) elementary 2-qubit quantum gate operations to find a marked node
equations.justification: Stated asymptotic cost in the abstract. The gate construction is not given.

equations.label: Grover coin
equations.description: Standard Grover diffusion coin on the d-dimensional coin space
equations.justification: Common coin choice in quantum walk search. The paper's coin is not stated.

equations.label: Walk step with marking
equations.description: The marked node gets coin -I instead of C, and the shift S then moves the walker
equations.justification: Standard coined-walk search construction. It is not the paper's explicit oracle-free circuit.
assumptions: Marking is realized by a coin modification

equations.label: Initial state
equations.description: Uniform superposition over positions and coins
equations.justification: Usual start state for walk search.

equations.label: Evolution and success probability
equations.description: State after T steps and the probability of measuring the marked node
equations.justification: Defines the figure of merit for choosing T.
assumptions: T is chosen near the first maximum of p_T

registers.name: pos
registers.size: ceil(log2 n) qubits (2 for the assumed 4-cycle)

specification.initial_state: Uniform superposition over pos and coin registers (eq_4), assumed.

steps.description: Prepare the uniform superposition with Hadamards.
Repeat T times: apply the marked coin, then the shift.
Measure the position register and estimate p_T.

specification.measurement: Computational-basis measurement of the position register, assumed.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Read the measured node as the candidate marked node, and verify it classically if needed.
assumptions: The 4-cycle with a Grover coin is an illustrative choice and is not from the abstract.
Equations 2 to 5 are generic background and not the paper's construction.

The derivation of the O(sqrt(n) log n) gate count
